note.text: Rotation is Earth's turning about its axis, approximately once per day. As a place turns into and out of sunlight, it experiences day and night. The apparent daily movement of the Sun across the sky is mainly a result of this rotation. Longitude-related local-time differences and the Coriolis effect are other consequences. Rotation is different from revolution around the Sun. The model used here treats the Sun's incoming rays as parallel.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Rotation is Earth's turning about its axis, approximately once per day. As a place turns into and out of sunlight, it experiences day and night. The apparent daily movement of the Sun across the sky is mainly a result of this rotation. Longitude-related local-time differences and the Coriolis effect are other consequences. Rotation is different from revolution around the Sun. The model used here treats the Sun's incoming rays as parallel.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: On the diagram, a town on the side facing the Sun is in daylight. A town turning toward the illuminated side experiences sunrise; one turning away experiences sunset. A pupil in Cameroon sees the daily change between light and darkness, but should not infer from that observation that the Sun travels around Earth each day.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the axis and direction of turning. Locate the lit half before deciding whether a marked town is in day or night. State which movement explains the effect: daily turning is rotation, while the yearly orbit is revolution.
